instructions: Cut the chicken into 1-inch pieces, pat them dry and season with the salt.

Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook, turning it now and then, until it's browned and cooked through, 6 to 7 minutes. You're cooking it to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into a piece: it's done when there's no pink left. Transfer it to a large bowl.
Add the diced onion and bell pepper to the same skillet and cook over medium heat, stirring, until the onion is soft and see-through, 3 to 4 minutes.
Transfer the vegetables to the bowl. Add the soup, tomatoes with their juice, broth, chili powder and garlic powder and stir well.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.

Spread 1/2 cup of the sauce over the bottom of an 8x8-inch baking dish. Cut 1 tortilla in half. Lay 2 whole tortillas and the 2 halves on the sauce, spoon over half of what's left in the bowl and sprinkle with 3/4 cup of the cheese.
Cut another tortilla in half and repeat the layer with the 4 remaining tortillas. Top with the rest of the sauce and the remaining 3/4 cup cheese.
Bake for 30 minutes, until it's bubbly and the cheese is lightly browned. Let it stand for 5 minutes, then cut it into squares.
Leftovers keep in the fridge for 4 days. Reheat them covered in a 350°F oven.
method_notes: Lead is Jo Cooks (4.5 from 56): a sauce of canned soup, tomatoes, chilies, chili powder and garlic powder, chicken and cheddar layered between corn tortillas. Amanda's Cookin' (5 from 9) is the same shape with sour cream. Halved from the lead's 9x13 dish to an 8x8, using cream of chicken soup alone and a can of tomatoes with green chiles in place of separate tomatoes and chilies. The chicken is cooked in the skillet from raw instead of using shredded cooked chicken, and the chive garnish is left out.
